why: The statement asks for a function modelling n-step self-avoiding walks; the linked article and its single reference point to counting c_n, so I read it as asking for a counting function (formula, algorithm or asymptotic) on the standard lattices. Exponent and displacement results (Hueter, Krachun-Panagiotis, OpenAI family 237) describe walk size, not counts, and are variants; weighted, self-osculating, cubic-graph and finite-grid restricted-step results are variants. Connective-constant results are bounds on a quantity in the count asymptotic (pre-snapshot). Lazar's 2025 preprint was the close call: c_n ~ I_n(0) is a reformulation as an unevaluated lattice-point integral with no error term and the step to the expected form left as a hope, so I scored it none rather than a case/whole claim. The two OpenAI rows are the same release (the second is a fuller reading of the same family); both are variant with role generated per the README quote.
doubts: The two OpenAI events duplicate one release. The statement is vague enough that a reader taking 'model' as any asymptotic description could score Lazar as a claimed whole and the OpenAI exponents as a case; I did not. Belbachir et al. has only a 2025 DOI year (after_snapshot null); Krachun-Panagiotis has no date of first written argument.
